roleAbout.text: Grace Wahba is Professor Emerita at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. UW identifies her smoothing-spline work as foundational to modern data science and machine learning.

lesson.text: A good model follows the signal while penalising needless wiggle: test whether extra detail improves the decision, not merely the fit.

roleAbout.text: Cynthia Dwork is Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science at Harvard SEAS, affiliated faculty at Harvard Law School and the Department of Statistics, and founder of the Hire Aspirations Institute.

lesson.text: Ask what can be learned about a group while making each person’s participation hard to infer: privacy is a measurable property, not a promise.

roleAbout.text: Daphne Koller is founder and CEO of insitro and remains an adjunct faculty member at Stanford, where her research page describes probabilistic models and machine learning for uncertain, complex domains.

lesson.text: When evidence is uncertain, represent alternatives and confidence instead of converting a guess into certainty.

roleAbout.text: MIT lists Barbara Liskov as an Institute Professor; EECS lists her as Institute Professor post-tenure. CSAIL identifies her as head of the Programming Methodology Group.

lesson.text: Put a clear interface around each component so its hidden implementation can change without breaking the people and systems that depend on it.

roleAbout.text: Jean Sammet was a Computer History Museum Fellow, a COBOL committee member, IBM’s FORMAC development leader, former ACM president and historian of programming languages. She died in 2017.

lesson.text: Languages and notation shape who can give precise instructions to a machine; usability is part of computing power.
